OMAHA, Neb.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Werner Enterprises, Inc. (Nasdaq: WERN), a premier transportation and logistics provider, today released its sixth annual sustainability report, the 2026 Sustainability Brief. The brief connects the company’s sustainability efforts with the operational priorities that matter to customers: reliable service, efficient freight movement and better visibility into supply chain emissions.

“For 70 years, Werner has helped keep America moving by investing in our people, our equipment and the service we deliver,” said Werner’s Chairman and CEO, Derek Leathers. “We are almost halfway to our goal of a 55% reduction in CO₂ emissions by 2035 against our 2020 baseline. Our sixth annual sustainability report highlights the practical investments in fleet efficiency, technology and emissions reporting that support our continued progress and help our customers meet their sustainability goals.”

Key highlights from the 2026 Sustainability Brief include:

  • Fleet Decarbonization & Equipment Innovation: Advanced a practical, multi-pathway decarbonization strategy by evaluating and piloting diverse low- and zero-emission technologies and fuels.
  • Emissions Reduction & Expanded Reporting: Achieved a 27% reduction in CO2 emissions relative to its 2020 baseline. Expanded transparency by refining Scope 1 and Scope 2 GHG accounting controls and disclosing Scope 3 supply chain emissions for the first time.
  • Waste Reduction & Environmental Stewardship: Utilized the Waste and Energy Scorecard to track resource efficiency, conserving more than 619,000 gallons of oil through tire retreading, recycling more than 850,000 pounds of metal and returning nearly 14,000 battery cores to production loops.
  • Strengthened Governance & Global Frameworks: Aligned reporting with SASB standards, UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and CDP climate disclosures. Established a formal Greenhouse Gas Inventory Management Plan (IMP) to prepare for future limited assurance reporting and mandatory compliance requirements.

The 2026 Sustainability Brief is available for download here.

About Werner Enterprises

Werner Enterprises, Inc. ("Werner") delivers superior truckload transportation and logistics services to customers across the United States, Mexico and Canada. With Werner® 2025 revenues of nearly $3.0 billion, a modern truck and trailer fleet, more than 14,800 talented associates and our innovative Werner EDGE® technology, we are an essential solutions provider for customers who value the integrity of their supply chain and require safe and exceptional on-time service. In January 2026, Werner acquired FirstEnterprises, Inc. ("FirstFleet"), which generated more than $600 million in unaudited 2025 revenues. Werner provides Dedicated and One-Way Truckload services as well as Logistics services that include truckload brokerage, freight management, intermodal and final mile. Werner embraces inclusion as a core value and manages key risks and opportunities through a balanced sustainability strategy.

Key Terms

scope 1technical
Scope 1 are the greenhouse gas emissions a company produces directly from sources it owns or controls, like fuel burned in company vehicles, boilers, or on-site factories. Think of it as the smoke coming out of a business’s own chimney versus electricity it buys from the grid. Investors watch Scope 1 because these direct emissions can create regulatory costs, operational changes, and reputational risks that affect profitability and long-term value.
scope 2technical
Scope 2 covers the greenhouse gas emissions produced indirectly when a business uses energy it buys from others—most commonly electricity, but also steam, heating or cooling. Think of it like the pollution linked to your household’s electricity bill: you didn’t burn the fuel yourself, but your consumption still causes emissions. Investors watch Scope 2 because it affects a company’s climate footprint, energy costs, regulatory exposure and reputation, all of which can influence long‑term financial performance.
scope 3technical
Scope 3 describes all greenhouse gas emissions that occur upstream and downstream of a company’s direct operations—things like emissions from suppliers, transportation, product use, and disposal. Think of it as the hidden carbon footprint tied to everything a business buys, sells, or enables; it matters to investors because these indirect emissions can drive regulatory costs, supply-chain disruption, consumer preference shifts, and long-term valuation risk that aren’t visible on a company’s factory floor or utility bill.
limited assuranceregulatory
An engagement where an independent auditor or reviewer provides moderate confidence that financial or non-financial information is free from material misstatement, but stops short of a full audit. Think of it as a focused check or review that uncovers obvious errors but does not involve the deep testing of a full audit. It matters to investors because it signals a lower level of independent verification of reported numbers, helping them judge how much trust to place in the disclosed information.

Third-quarter EBITDA increases 99% over the preceding quarter to $197,733

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 20, 2026) - Metaguest.AI Incorporated (CSE: METG) ("Metaguest" or the "Company"), an AI technology company transforming the hospitality sector through intelligent guest engagement, announces its unaudited financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, together with the results of its Annual General and Special Meeting of Shareholders held on November 19, 2026.

Metaguest reported EBITDA of $197,733 for the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 99.2% from $99,273 in the second quarter, marking its second consecutive quarter of positive EBITDA. Adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter was $190,179. EBITDA for the corresponding quarter of 2025 was $(328,288).

The Company also recorded net income of $66,734 for the third quarter, compared with a net loss of $494,449 in Q3 2025.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, EBITDA improved to $237,282, compared with $(858,506) in 2025. Adjusted EBITDA was $220,613. The Company's nine-month net loss decreased by approximately 86%, from $1,305,425 to $180,748.

These improvements reflect the Company's ongoing cost-management initiatives, organizational changes and strengthened financial oversight.

Management Commentary

Colin Keddy, President and Director of Metaguest, commented:

"Our third-quarter results reflect the progress we have made in strengthening the Company's financial and operating structure. Achieving a second consecutive quarter of positive EBITDA, with a substantial increase over the preceding quarter, demonstrates the impact of our efforts to streamline operations and manage costs while maintaining our established hotel distribution network.

"With a more disciplined operating structure in place, we are now focused on advancing our technology, enhancing the digital guest experience and developing additional revenue opportunities across our hotel network.

"We recognize that these initiatives will require further investment and may affect profitability in future periods. Our objective is to balance those investments with responsible financial management as we work toward building a stronger and more scalable business."

Hotel Partner Network and Development

Metaguest has established a network of approximately 475 hotel partners across the United States and Canada, providing an existing distribution platform through which the Company intends to expand merchant participation, guest engagement and commercial opportunities.

Management intends to enhance the platform through AI-assisted services, personalized recommendations and additional digital guest engagement capabilities. These initiatives are expected to require further development expenditures, subject to available financing and technical feasibility.

As the Company increases investment in technology and development, operating expenditures may rise and could result in net losses in future periods. Management believes these investments are important to supporting the Company's longer-term growth and monetization strategy.

The Company continues to manage its liquidity and creditor obligations while evaluating additional financing opportunities. Material uncertainty remains regarding its ability to continue as a going concern, as disclosed in its interim financial statements.

Annual General and Special Meeting Results

The Company also announces that its Annual General and Special Meeting of Shareholders was held on November 19, 2026. All motions presented to shareholders at the meeting were approved.

The Company thanks its shareholders for their continued support.

Non-IFRS Financial Measures

EBITDA is calculated as net income or loss before interest and accretion, income taxes, depreciation and amortization. Adjusted EBITDA is calculated as EBITDA adjusted to exclude gains or losses arising from the recognition, derecognition or modification of financial instruments.

About Metaguest.AI Incorporated

Metaguest.AI is a next-generation technology company focused on enhancing the guest experience through advanced AI solutions. Its flagship platform provides an end-to-end guest engagement ecosystem, covering everything from pre-arrival to post-departure. Features include on-property e-commerce with digital payments, real-time service requests, mobile check-out, personalized in-room controls, local experience and event bookings, and a multilingual virtual concierge, all accessible without downloading an app or visiting a website. JOHANNESBURG, South Africa, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- ProText Mobility, Inc. (OTC: TXTM) today presents a comprehensive strategic shareholder update from its Chairman and President, Dr. Ahmed Jamaloodeen, addressing the Company’s real-world asset foundation, proprietary biotechnology, agricultural production, digital tokenisation infrastructure, institutional banking relationships, international strategic initiatives, financial reporting programme and regulated-exchange roadmap.

The Chairman’s statement provides an integrated overview of the Company’s established capabilities, recent implementation milestones and strategic priorities for translating its asset base and commercial relationships into revenue, profitability and long-term shareholder value.

A MESSAGE FROM DR AHMED JAMALOODEEN, Chairman and President:

DEAR FELLOW SHAREHOLDERS, PROSPECTIVE INVESTORS AND MARKET PARTICIPANTS,

I believe it is important to provide shareholders with a comprehensive understanding of what has been assembled at ProText Mobility, Inc., how the various components connect and the economic significance of our broader corporate strategy.

Over the past several years, we have brought together substantial real-world assets, agricultural production capabilities, proprietary biotechnology, pharmaceutical-related inventory, digital tokenisation infrastructure, institutional financial relationships and international commercial opportunities.

We have also established important corporate reporting, investor-relations and information-technology infrastructure.

These are not disconnected initiatives.

They form an integrated business ecosystem designed to create, enhance, administer and monetise real-world economic assets.

Our strategy has always extended beyond one product, one technology, one token or one transaction.

And it begins with an important distinction.

WE ARE NOT STARTING FROM ZERO.

We have existing assets.

We have established technologies.

We have demonstrated agricultural multiplication.

We have pharmaceutical-related inventory.

We have deployed digital infrastructure.

We have institutional banking relationships.

We have agreed financial arrangements.

We have international commercial relationships developed over decades.

And we have an existing publicly traded company through which qualifying economic opportunities can be developed.

The next stage of our roadmap is focused on translating these components into measurable revenue, profitability and long-term shareholder value.

1. OUR EXISTING REAL-WORLD ASSET FOUNDATION

ProText Mobility’s previously published financial statements already reflect substantial real-world assets.

As of June 30, 2026, the Company reported approximately:

1.9 BILLION AGRICULTURAL SEEDS

With a recorded carrying value of approximately: US$605 MILLION.

Separately, in September 2025, True Leaf Holdings (TruLeaf) contributed:

125,959,995 MILLIGRAMS OF ACTIVE PHARMACEUTICAL INGREDIENTS.

The Company’s financial disclosures recorded these APIs at the contributor’s historical cost of approximately US$6.298 million under US GAAP.

The contribution also had an estimated fair market value of approximately US$10.71 million at the time.

These figures represent previously disclosed accounting and valuation measures, rather than cash balances or completed monetisation proceeds.

The significance of these assets extends beyond their reported financial values.

They provide an established economic foundation for our biotechnology, agricultural and digital financial infrastructure.

REAL ASSETS UNDERPIN THE BUSINESS.

2. AGRICULTURAL MULTIPLICATION — ADDITIONAL ASSETS THROUGH PRODUCTION

Our seed multiplication agreement was established in October 2023.

Through this arrangement, qualifying seed inventory has undergone planting, germination, harvesting, processing and subsequent return to the Company.

Multiple completed production cycles have been documented in our financial disclosures.

During the first quarter of 2026 alone, the Company recorded an increase of approximately 300 million seeds through its established multiplication programme.

This is an accomplished agricultural activity.

The economic principle is straightforward.

EXISTING BIOLOGICAL ASSETS CAN PRODUCE ADDITIONAL BIOLOGICAL ASSETS.

Our Chairman’s independent agricultural operations and related commercial arrangements provide access to longstanding farming experience, infrastructure and production capabilities.

These resources have been developed over generations.

The relevant assets, permits and contractual relationships are distinguished according to their legal ownership and the Company’s public disclosures.

The multiplication programme demonstrates the productive foundation supporting our asset-development strategy.

But increasing the quantity of assets is only one component.

An equally important component is increasing their commercial value.

3. KETTLE TECHNOLOGY AND NANOTECHNOLOGY — ENHANCING ECONOMIC VALUE

This is where our proprietary biotechnology connects directly with our real-world asset and financial infrastructure.

ProText Mobility’s Kettle technology and live-plant extraction capabilities are established components of our biotechnology platform.

The Company’s relationship with TruLeaf adds complementary nanotechnology and pharmaceutical-related expertise.

These capabilities create pathways for transforming qualifying biological materials into extracts, cannabinoid-related APIs and differentiated formulations.

Nanotechnology provides opportunities to enhance the bioavailability and delivery characteristics of suitable formulations.

The commercial importance of this combination is substantial.

OUR BUSINESS IS NOT LIMITED TO INCREASING THE NUMBER OF PHYSICAL ASSETS.

We also have technological capabilities relevant to increasing the economic value generated from qualifying biological materials.

A raw agricultural input, a refined extract and a specialised pharmaceutical-related formulation can possess substantially different commercial applications and values.

Where processing, quality verification, product performance and market demand support such differences, the resulting economic value can be independently assessed.

Our business therefore incorporates two complementary value-creation mechanisms.

ASSET MULTIPLICATION

Producing additional biological assets through established agricultural processes.

ASSET VALUE ENHANCEMENT

Applying Kettle extraction and complementary nanotechnology to develop commercially differentiated products.

This is a fundamental component of our broader strategy.

WE HAVE THE PHYSICAL ASSETS.

WE HAVE THE TECHNOLOGY.

WE HAVE THE PRODUCTION CAPABILITIES.

These components connect directly with our digital tokenisation infrastructure.

4. TRULEAF — A SEPARATE PHARMACEUTICAL-RELATED ASSET BASE

The TruLeaf API contribution introduced an additional category of physical assets into TXTM’s reported inventory.

It also strengthened the connection between our agricultural activities, biotechnology capabilities and pharmaceutical-related opportunities.

The existing API contribution provides an additional foundation for appropriate commercial applications involving biological materials, specialised extracts and formulated products.

Kettle technology and complementary nanotechnology provide established technological capabilities relevant to this value chain.

TXTM IS NOT SIMPLY A SEED-INVENTORY BUSINESS.

Its broader ecosystem encompasses agricultural production, biotechnology, cannabinoid-related APIs, digital infrastructure and financial applications.

The integration of these capabilities is central to the Company’s identity.

5. THE CONNECTION BETWEEN RWA VALUE AND TOKEN VALUE

One of the most important features of our strategy is the relationship between underlying physical economic value and digital asset representation.

Our existing agricultural multiplication programme has demonstrated the production of additional inventory.

Our biotechnology capabilities provide pathways for enhancing the commercial value of qualifying biological materials.

Our tokenisation infrastructure connects eligible underlying assets with digital financial applications.

This creates two potential mechanisms for increasing the asset value represented within an appropriately structured token programme.

FIRST: Additional independently verified underlying assets.

SECOND: Increased independently supportable value of qualifying underlying assets.

For example, additional verified seed inventory may support further authorised token issuance.

Separately, higher-value commercial outputs may support a revised asset valuation or an additional tokenisation structure, depending upon the legal rights represented.

Changes in underlying economic value can be reflected in the applicable token’s independently determined net asset value where its governing methodology permits.

Such changes do not automatically establish a higher market trading price.

THE VALUE ORIGINATES WITH THE UNDERLYING ECONOMIC ASSETS.

The tokenisation infrastructure provides the mechanism for their digital representation and financial administration.

This principle also extends to other eligible real-world asset classes, including verified environmental assets and carbon credits.

6. SVLT — DEPLOYED DIGITAL ASSET INFRASTRUCTURE

The Seed Vault Token programme is an established component of our ecosystem.

SVLT has been deployed using an ERC-3643 permissioned architecture incorporating identity, compliance and administrative functionality.

The Company’s agricultural seed-tokenisation initiative has already been publicly announced.

The infrastructure has been developed to support the digital representation of qualifying real-world assets.

Its importance lies in connecting tangible economic resources with appropriate verification, governance and institutional financial systems.

SVLT is not being presented as a speculative public token sale.

Its role within our strategy is the digital representation and administration of defined asset-related rights.

The broader tokenisation architecture can also support evaluation of additional qualifying asset classes.

TOKENISATION IS AN ENABLER OF ECONOMIC VALUE — NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR IT.

7. OUR DIGITAL DASHBOARD AND INFORMATION-TECHNOLOGY ECOSYSTEM

Our digital dashboard and broader information-technology infrastructure are established components of the business.

They provide the technological foundation for asset information, digital administration and the integration of appropriate financial applications.

The business model encompasses two complementary activities.

TXTM-RELATED ASSETS

Qualifying assets owned by the Company and developed through its commercial activities.

THIRD-PARTY ASSET SERVICES

Digital asset administration, tokenisation and related technology services for qualifying third-party asset owners.

This distinction is significant.

Traditional asset-management businesses may generate revenue by managing assets that belong to others.

Our model combines that potential service opportunity with an existing base of physical assets and productive capabilities.

The objective is to generate commercial value from both asset-related activities and financial infrastructure services.

The ownership of third-party assets remains separate from TXTM’s own balance sheet.

8. ABSA — ESTABLISHED INSTITUTIONAL CUSTODY AND AGREED FINANCIAL ARRANGEMENTS

In September 2026, the Company publicly announced that ABSA had confirmed the Chairman’s participation as its inaugural pilot client in the bank’s digital-asset custody onboarding programme.

The relevant onboarding, approvals, documentation and signatures are complete.

The Chairman’s profile is ready on the system.

ABSA has confirmed: “Your profile is ready on the system.”

The custody wallet is established and ready specifically to receive SVLT.

ABSA CUSTODY ONBOARDING IS COMPLETE.

THE PROFILE IS READY. THE SVLT WALLET IS READY.

The platform walkthrough is now being coordinated as part of operational execution, followed by the first SVLT test transfer.

This is a demonstration of the established system and its operation.

In addition, the Chairman confirms that institutional trading and monetisation arrangements have been agreed with ABSA.

THE AGREEMENT STAGE IS NOT BEING DESCRIBED AS AN ASPIRATION.

THE ARRANGEMENTS ARE AGREED. WE ARE EXECUTING NOW.

The focus is on implementing those arrangements, completing and verifying relevant digital asset transfers, and reporting commercial transactions and financial results as they occur.

Institutional custody is an established component of our broader asset-backed financial infrastructure.

THE FOUNDATION IS ESTABLISHED. THE INFRASTRUCTURE IS IN PLACE. EXECUTION CONTINUES.

8A. TXTM COMMON AND PREFERRED STOCK TOKENISATION — SMART CONTRACT COMPLETED

Separate from SVLT, our TXTM equity-tokenisation programme is moving forward with implementation.

The programme encompasses the Chairman’s personally held TXTM common and preferred stock.

Our technical implementation partner has confirmed completion of the smart contract for the TXTM token.

THE SMART CONTRACT IS COMPLETE.

The requested brokerage statements and supporting ownership documentation covering the Chairman’s personally held common and preferred stock have been submitted.

Receipt has been confirmed.

DOCUMENTATION SENT. RECEIPT CONFIRMED.

The next step is the deployment walkthrough for the TXTM token.

This programme concerns the digital representation and administration of existing equity-related interests.

It is distinct from SVLT and the tokenisation of agricultural or other physical assets.

The underlying common and preferred stock already exists.

Tokenisation of these existing interests does not itself issue additional TXTM common shares or convert the Chairman’s preferred stock into common shares.

The legal and economic rights represented by the tokens will be governed by the applicable transaction documentation, with the underlying ownership records and transfer requirements preserved.

This adds a separate equity-related component to our established digital infrastructure and broader capital-markets programme.

EXISTING COMMON AND PREFERRED STOCK.

SMART CONTRACT COMPLETED.

OWNERSHIP DOCUMENTATION RECEIVED.

DEPLOYMENT WALKTHROUGH NEXT.

9. BNY MELLON, OTHER BANKING INSTITUTIONS AND THE FAMILY OFFICE

Our institutional relationships extend beyond ABSA.

The Chairman maintains an existing direct account relationship with BNY Mellon.

This is a direct BNY relationship and is separate from the ABSA custody initiative.

The Chairman also confirms additional established relationships and agreed financial arrangements involving other banking institutions.

These relationships have been developed through longstanding commercial and institutional engagement.

The family office provides an established international network, financial relationships, credit resources and commercial experience.

These capabilities have developed over many years.

They are part of the broader institutional foundation supporting the Chairman’s international business activities.

Personal and family-office accounts, credit facilities and assets remain legally distinct from those of TXTM unless expressly committed to the Company under applicable agreements.

The significance is that the broader ecosystem is supported by existing financial relationships and commercial experience rather than depending entirely on newly introduced institutional contacts.

WE HAVE THE RELATIONSHIPS.

WE HAVE THE EXPERIENCE.

WE HAVE THE FINANCIAL CONNECTIVITY.

10. INSURANCE WRAPS, PERFORMANCE GUARANTEES AND INSTITUTIONAL MONETISATION

Insurance and contractual performance protections form another component of our financial strategy.

The Chairman confirms that valuation documentation, auditor support and insurance arrangements have been assembled.

The financial architecture incorporates insurance-wrap and performance-guarantee considerations relevant to specified contractual obligations.

These arrangements can support the management of defined financial and counterparty risks according to their governing terms.

Our broader financial strategy connects qualifying real-world assets, valuation, digital representation, institutional custody and collateral arrangements.

These components support the implementation of agreed institutional financial structures.

Specific financial obligations, coverage limits, beneficiaries and payment terms remain governed by the relevant contracts.

The intended economic result is the generation of lawful contractual revenue and financial proceeds through completed commercial transactions.

Revenue is recognised by the appropriate entity when the underlying transactions and accounting requirements support recognition.

OUR FOCUS IS ASSET-BACKED MONETISATION AND MEASURABLE FINANCIAL RESULTS.

11. CARBON CREDITS — AN ADDITIONAL REAL-WORLD ASSET OPPORTUNITY

Our asset strategy extends beyond agricultural seeds and pharmaceutical-related inventory.

Environmental assets and carbon credits represent another important component.

This is directly relevant to our existing agricultural capabilities, sustainability initiatives and international commercial relationships.

Qualifying environmental projects may generate recognised carbon credits or other environmental attributes through approved methodologies and independent verification.

Such credits can be administered, transferred, tokenised or commercially monetised where permitted.

The underlying principle remains consistent with our broader real-world asset strategy.

12. REGENERATIVE AGRICULTURE, ZERO-WASTE AND THE CIRCULAR ECONOMY

Our agricultural philosophy extends beyond crop production.

It incorporates environmental stewardship, regenerative farming principles, soil preservation and responsible resource management.

Our broader practices and project frameworks include no-till agriculture where suitable, resource-efficient production and opportunities for biological and environmental restoration.

These approaches connect naturally with our zero-waste and circular-economy philosophy.

Agricultural residues and appropriate processing by-products can have additional commercial applications.

Rather than treating all residual materials as waste, our model recognises opportunities for resource recovery and productive reuse.

Examples within our broader project portfolio include biomass utilisation, biogas, renewable power, agricultural fertiliser and water recovery.

Where appropriate, these activities may also support independently verified environmental attributes.

This approach connects agricultural productivity with potential environmental and economic benefits.

It is also relevant to international sustainability frameworks, environmental, social and governance principles, and national climate commitments associated with the United Nations climate COP process and 2030 development objectives.

Our environmental strategy seeks to connect responsible resource management with commercially viable activity.

SUSTAINABILITY AND ECONOMIC VALUE CREATION CAN REINFORCE ONE ANOTHER.

13. VENEZUELA — AGRICULTURE, ENERGY AND THE CIRCULAR ECONOMY

The Chairman’s longstanding relationships in Venezuela provide an established foundation for international project development.

The government-related pilot and LOI framework includes opportunities involving agricultural production, biological resources and circular-economy infrastructure.

The project framework connects rice production with agricultural residue utilisation, biogas, renewable energy, fertiliser and water recovery.

Additional opportunities may include qualifying environmental assets and related energy applications.

These activities are part of a broader international development model that connects agricultural production, resource efficiency and commercial infrastructure.

The Chairman’s personal government-related arrangements remain legally distinct from agreements entered into directly by TXTM.

The Company’s economic participation in any resulting project will be governed by the relevant commercial documentation.

The Venezuela initiative also illustrates the significance of our existing Latin American and Caribbean relationships.

These relationships contribute to broader regional opportunities involving international commerce, financial infrastructure, agriculture and real-world assets.

14. INTERNATIONAL STRATEGIC RELATIONSHIPS, LOIs AND JOINT VENTURES

DOVER, USA, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- E-Power Inc. (“E-Power,” the “Company,” “we” or “our”) (NASDAQ: EPOW), a provider of advanced battery materials and AI Data Center (AIDC) microgrid solutions, today announced that its joint venture, Sunrise (Guizhou) New Energy Materials Co., Ltd. (“Sunrise Guizhou”), has been designated a national-level Specialized, Refined, Distinctive and Innovative (“Little Giant”) enterprise by China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (“MIIT”) as part of the MIIT’s eighth batch of Little Giant designations. Sunrise Guizhou received notice of the designation on October 14, 2026 through the MIIT’s High-Quality SME Gradient Cultivation Platform.

The designation completes the national review process described in the Company’s press release of August 20, 2026, which announced that Sunrise Guizhou had passed provincial review by the Department of Industry and Information Technology of Guizhou Province and was one of 28 enterprises included in the province’s recommendation list for the eighth batch.

The Top Tier of China’s SME Cultivation System

The MIIT’s gradient cultivation system for high-quality small and medium-sized enterprises (“SMEs”) has three tiers: technology-based and innovative SMEs; specialized and sophisticated SMEs, recognized at the provincial level; and Little Giant enterprises, designated at the national level by the MIIT. Only enterprises that already hold provincial specialized and sophisticated SME status may apply for Little Giant designation. The program recognizes SMEs that focus on specific market segments, possess core technologies and strong innovation capabilities, and hold leading positions in their segments.

Applications for the eighth batch were assessed under the MIIT’s revised Measures for the Administration of Gradient Cultivation of High-Quality Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises, issued in January 2026. According to the MIIT’s notice to Sunrise Guizhou, the designation followed preliminary review and recommendation by local authorities, expert review, and internal deliberation by the MIIT. The MIIT’s review uses staged review, random assignment of experts and review tasks, and blind review, and cross-checks application data using data analysis tools. The designation is valid for three years, from July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2029.

Progression Through All Three Tiers

Sunrise Guizhou has advanced through each tier of the system. It was recognized as an innovative SME in April 2023 and as a specialized and sophisticated SME in July 2024, and in May 2025 it was designated a Guizhou Province Key Specialized and Sophisticated SME. The Little Giant designation places it in the system’s top tier.

Sunrise Guizhou manufactures graphite anode materials and develops next-generation anode materials, including silicon-carbon composites and hard carbon for sodium-ion batteries. It was certified as a National High-Tech Enterprise in 2023. In 2024, one of its projects was selected through the “Open Competition” (Jie Bang Gua Shuai) mechanism of an MIIT industrial foundation innovation program and passed final acceptance in December 2024. In May 2025, it received an Excellence Award at the 25th China Patent Awards, granted by the China National Intellectual Property Administration, and in 2026 it participated in drafting the national standard “Porous Carbon for Silicon-Based Anode Materials” (Plan No. 20262157-T-605).

“This designation completes the national review that followed Guizhou’s provincial recommendation earlier this year, and we see it as recognition of our Guizhou team’s long-standing focus on anode materials,” said Mr. Haiping Hu, the founder, CEO and Chairman of E-Power Inc. “Because the designation is reviewed every three years, we intend to keep earning it through continued investment in research, standards work and manufacturing quality.”

About E-Power Inc.

E-Power Inc., through its subsidiaries, joint venture and variable interest entity structure, is engaged in the manufacturing and sale of graphite anode material for lithium-ion batteries. Through its joint venture, the Company operates a plant in Guizhou Province, China, powered by electricity from renewable sources, which contributes to the plant’s competitive production costs and reduced environmental impact in the production of graphite anode material. Mr. Haiping Hu, the founder, CEO and Chairman of the Company, has been a pioneer in the graphite anode industry since 1999. The Company’s management team is composed of experts with years of experience and successful track records in the graphite anode industry. Analysis of credit card transactions finds that sporting goods purchases ramp up earlier than other categories, driven in part by hunting season

MINNEAPOLIS--(BUSINESS WIRE)--

Based on an analysis of credit card transactions processed across a sample of about 50,000 small- and medium-sized retail merchants from 2022 through 2025, Deluxe Corporation (NYSE: DLX) found that while sporting-goods retailers who carry hunting equipment bagged their biggest haul around Thanksgiving, beauty, apparel, and accessory purchases increased sharply in the final two weeks before Christmas.

The boost in sporting goods transactions is likely due to the start of hunting season overlapping with Black Friday in many states, as well as to end-of-year rebates offered by hunting and outdoor adventure equipment manufacturers. In contrast, transactions involving beauty services, apparel, and accessories saw substantially larger increases when Christmas shopping was down to the wire.

These category-specific patterns take on added importance in a year when many consumers are managing tighter budgets. The 2026 Consumer Holiday Spending Study from The Strawhecker Group and the Electronic Transactions Association found that 44% of consumers report greater financial stress than last year and 72% plan to set a holiday budget. With shoppers more deliberate about when and how much they spend, knowing which categories peak early versus late can help retailers make sharper decisions on inventory, staffing, and promotions.

“This is a great example of how the combination of Celero and Deluxe can transform data into useful insights for our customers and partners,” said Kevin Jones, president of Deluxe Merchant Services. “Understanding how and when consumers spend empowers businesses to make better decisions about staffing, inventory, and marketing, and we’re in a great position to help small- and medium-sized businesses interpret the data Deluxe has accumulated.”

Across all retail categories analyzed, the increase in transactions between Thanksgiving week and the mid-December shopping period narrowed substantially over the four-year study. In 2022, average transactions per merchant were 17% higher during the peak Christmas shopping week than during Thanksgiving week. That difference narrowed to 16% in 2023 and just 1% in 2024, before recovering modestly to 4% in 2025.

In 2025:

  • Beauty services: Average transactions per merchant increased 18% in the week before Christmas compared with Thanksgiving week.
  • Apparel and accessories: Average transactions per merchant increased 20% during Christmas week compared with Thanksgiving week.
  • Sporting goods stores processed approximately 18.9% more payment volume per merchant during Thanksgiving week in 2025 than their average weekly volume during the two weeks leading up to Christmas.

The same TSG/ETA study found that 57% of consumers would shop elsewhere or be less likely to return if their preferred payment method wasn’t available—reinforcing that capturing concentrated late-season demand also requires offering the payment options shoppers expect.

Tips to Protect Pipes Before Freezing Temperatures

ALEXANDRIA, Va., Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- As winter approaches, Virginia American Water reminds customers to prepare their home and pipes, providing handy tips to help avoid costly repairs and unwanted stress from frozen pipes. 

"Customers should prepare for frigid temperatures by taking simple steps to protect their pipes from freezing," said Charlie Piekanski, Vice President of Operations, Virginia American Water. "By taking proactive measures, you can help ensure you and your loved ones stay safe and comfortable when the temperature drops."  

You can prepare now by taking the following steps:  

  • Know how to shut off your water: Locate your main water shut-off valve. In many homes, it is located near the water meter or close to where the water pipe enters the home. Hang an I.D. tag on the valve so it can be found quickly during an emergency. Download a tag to print here.
  • Test your main water shut-off valve: Once located, test the shut-off valve by closing it. Once completely closed, check sinks and other water fixtures to ensure the shut-off valve is working properly.  
    • Ball valves generally only require a quarter turn to close. 
    • Gate valves are generally closed by turning the handle clockwise and should turn easily.  
    • If the valve does not close easily, it may need to be serviced.  
    • Bonus: While you are there, check your incoming water service line material! Virginia American Water is working with customers to identify their service line material. If it is found to be made of lead or galvanized steel, they will be replaced in the future. Visit our website for information.  
  • Check sprinkler or irrigation systems: Make sure everything is turned off and fully drained. 
  • Eliminate sources of cold air near water lines: Check for pipes in areas that might be prone to freezing, such as crawl spaces, unheated rooms, basements, garages, and exterior walls. Fix drafty windows, insulate walls around pipes and plug drafts around doors. 
  • Protect your pipes: Where pipes are exposed to cold, wrap them with insulation or heat tape (even fabric or newspaper can help). 

When temperatures stay below freezing: 

  • Give pipes a helping hand: If pipes run through cabinets or vanities, open the doors to let warmer room temperatures flow in. 
  • Keep water moving through the pipes: Allow a small trickle of water to run. The cost of the extra water is typically lower than the cost of repairing a broken pipe. 

If pipes freeze:  

  • Shut off the water immediately: Do not attempt to thaw pipes without turning off the main water shut-off valve. 
  • Thaw a frozen pipe by warming the air around it: Use a hair dryer, space heater or hot water. Do not leave space heaters unattended and avoid using kerosene heaters or open flames.  
  • Once pipes are thawed: Slowly turn the water back on. Check pipes and joints for any cracks or leaks potentially caused by freezing.  

When customers are away from home, consider the following: 

  • Set your thermostat at 55 degrees to prevent freezing. 
  • Have a friend, relative or neighbor regularly check the property to help ensure the heat is working and the pipes have not frozen.  
  • Consider purchasing a freeze alarm. The alarm will call a user-selected phone number if the inside temperature drops below 45 degrees. 

Find cold weather protection tips here: https://amwater.com/corp/Customers-and-Communities/Wise-Water-Use/cold-weather-protection.

Key Terms

form s-1regulatory
A Form S-1 is the registration filing a company submits to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission when it plans to offer stock to the public, most commonly for an initial public offering. Think of it as the company’s full disclosure packet or blueprint: it contains audited financials, business description, management background, risk factors and details of the offering, giving investors the information needed to judge the company’s financial health and potential risks before buying shares.
equity line of creditfinancial
An equity line of credit is a loan that allows homeowners to borrow money against the value of their property, similar to having a flexible credit card secured by their home. It matters to investors because it provides a way for property owners to access cash for various needs, which can influence real estate markets and overall economic activity. This type of credit offers ongoing borrowing capacity, making it a valuable financial tool for those with significant property equity.
senior credit facilityfinancial
A senior credit facility is a large loan or revolving line of credit that a company borrows from banks or lenders and that has first claim on the company’s cash and assets if the business runs into financial trouble. Think of it as the “first in line” debt with stronger repayment priority and usually stricter rules, so investors watch it because its size, cost and covenants affect a company’s cash flow, risk profile and the value of equity and other creditors.
stockholders' equityfinancial
Stockholders' equity is the portion of a company's assets that belongs to its owners after all debts and obligations are paid; think of it as the value left for shareholders if the company sold everything and paid off what it owes. Investors watch it because it shows the company's net worth, indicates how much of growth is funded by owners versus debt, and helps assess financial health and the potential for future dividends or stock value increases — like the equity in a house after the mortgage is settled.

Black Friday offer and holiday promo codes aimed at the half of U.S. shoppers planning to give an experience this season

FORT WORTH, Texas, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Sports Entertainment Gaming Global Corporation ("SEGG Media" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: SEGG) today announced that TicketStub.com will relaunch on a new platform on November 25, at the start of the holiday shopping season. TicketStub.com will open with a Black Friday offer, with details to be announced closer to launch, and will release promo codes for discounted tickets throughout the holidays.

Half of U.S. holiday shoppers plan to give an experience this year, up from 39% in 2024, and 19% plan to give tickets to an event, according to Deloitte's 2026 Holiday Retail Survey. The same survey found that 47% of shoppers would rather give one meaningful, higher-cost gift than several smaller ones. On the receiving side, concert tickets ranked second only to a full trip among the experiences Americans most wanted as a holiday gift, cited by 51% of respondents in a 2025 Talker Research survey of 5,000 adults commissioned by Chime.

Demand for live events is running at record levels. Live Nation Entertainment reported selling 170 million concert tickets through October 2026, up 13% year over year and already ahead of its total for all of 2025.

TicketStub.com gives users access to thousands of events around the world and earns revenue through service fees. The Company plans to add advertising and promoted listings as the platform develops. The relaunch follows the worldwide relaunch of Lottery.com on November 18 and is supported by the strategic financing commitments SEGG Media announced on November 12.

"Veloce's channels draw more than 500 million views a month from fans who follow racing, gaming and live sport. That's an audience that goes to live events, and putting TicketStub.com in front of them is our first priority," said Gregory Potts, Chief Operating Officer of SEGG Media. "We also plan to add an ongoing sweepstakes where users can win free tickets, concert experiences and other live event prizes. Along with the Black Friday offer and holiday promo codes, it gives fans a reason to keep coming back to TicketStub.com."

SEGG Media (Nasdaq: SEGG, LTRYW) is a global sports, entertainment, and gaming group operating a portfolio of digital assets including Sports.com, Concerts.com, TicketStub.com, Lottery.com, and Veloce Media Group. Tokyo, Japan, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Tokyo Lifestyle Co., Ltd. (“Tokyo Lifestyle” or the “Company”) (Nasdaq: TKLF), a retailer and wholesaler of Japanese beauty and health products, sundry products, luxury products, electronic products, collectible cards, trendy toys as well as other products in Hong Kong, Japan, North America, Thailand, Vietnam, the United Kingdom and Australia, today announced the planned opening of a new store under its proprietary “Reiwatakiya” brand (the “Store”) in London, the United Kingdom, on November 21, 2026. This expansion marks another important milestone in the Company’s ongoing efforts to strengthen its UK retail presence, broaden its customer reach, and enhance its international sales network.

A Prime Retail Location in an Iconic Shopping Destination

Located at Westfield London, one of the largest shopping centers in the UK and Europe, the new Reiwatakiya Store is expected to benefit from substantial shopper traffic and a diverse international customer base. Supported by convenient transportation links, including underground, rail, and road networks, Westfield London and its surrounding area attract approximately 27.9 million visitors annually. The shopping center generates approximately £1 billion in annual retail sales, underscoring its position as a leading commercial and retail destination in London.

The Store will showcase Tokyo Lifestyle’s diverse selection of authentic Japanese beauty and lifestyle products, selected Korean beauty brands. Strategically situated next to Zara and Apple stores, the Store is positioned to attract a broad consumer audience, particularly younger shoppers who represent an important target demographic for the Company.

To celebrate its grand opening on November 21 and 22, the Store will host special promotional activities, including a limited-time Japanese beauty goodie bag giveaway. These initiatives are designed to attract initial customer traffic, build brand awareness and foster engagement with local consumers. For more details about the grand opening event, please visit https://reiwatakiya.co.uk/.

The new Store will complement Tokyo Lifestyle’s existing London location in the city center, strengthening its retail presence in distinct commercial areas across the city. Together, these locations are expected to enhance the Company’s brand visibility, broaden its access to local consumers and international visitors, and provide a stronger operating foundation for potential expansion into other European markets.

Advancing Global Expansion Through a Distinctive Retail Brand Strategy

The Company’s UK expansion forms part of its broader global growth strategy, guided by its commitment to bringing authentic Japanese beauty and lifestyle products, distinctive cultural experiences, and emerging consumer trends to customers worldwide. In recent years, Tokyo Lifestyle has accelerated the expansion of its international retail operations, with its latest physical store opening in Sydney in October 2026.

Alongside its expanding international retail footprint, the Company continues to pursue greater revenue diversification and brand development through a combination of directly operated stores, franchise partnerships, and wholesale distribution channels. These initiatives are intended to strengthen its international market presence, broaden its customer base, and establish a more diversified and scalable global business platform.

Mr. Mei Kanayama, Principal Executive Officer of Tokyo Lifestyle, commented: “The opening of our new Reiwatakiya store in the UK represents an important milestone in our long-term commitment to the UK and broader European markets. London has long served as a strategic gateway for our European expansion, and establishing two retail locations in distinct commercial areas across the city will enable us to reach a wider customer base, strengthen our brand recognition, and further develop our local operating capabilities.

“We have made a meaningful long-term commitment to this location, reflecting our confidence in the commercial potential of Westfield London and the continued appeal of Japanese beauty and lifestyle products among international consumers. Beyond adding another retail location, we see this Store as an opportunity to further refine our retail positioning, deepen customer engagement, and strengthen our understanding of local consumer preferences. Looking ahead, we intend to leverage our growing presence in London as a foundation for exploring additional opportunities across the UK and Europe, while continuing to build a distinctive and internationally recognized retail brand. We believe our expanding global retail network, combined with our diversified product portfolio and multi-channel business model, will position Tokyo Lifestyle to capture emerging market opportunities and generate sustainable long-term value for our shareholders.”
